PullRequest.Title: Git - keep tag conflict dialog short and chunk forced tag fetch
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #205369

## Repro steps

1. Create a bare "remote" repository with many tags (the evidence below uses 7,500 lightweight tags named like `release/v1.00001.0-nightly-build-candidate-linux-x64-signed-artifacts`) pointing at commit `B` (history `A -> B`).
2. Clone it, then move every local tag to commit `A` (`git update-ref --stdin` / `git tag -f`, then `git pack-refs --all`).
3. Push a new commit `C` to the remote so there is something to pull.
4. Open the clone in VS Code (`"window.dialogStyle": "custom"` so the dialog is rendered in the DOM) and run **Git: Pull** (`git.pullTags` is on by default).
5. 🐛 The "conflicting tag(s)" modal lists all 7,500 tag names (~530K characters). The message fills the dialog and the "Always Replace Local Tag(s)" / "Cancel" / "Replace Local Tag(s)" buttons are squeezed and clipped at its bottom edge (each only ~62% visible). The issue reports the buttons going off-screen with the native dialog as well.
6. 🐛 Choosing **Replace Local Tag(s)** fails with `Git: spawn E2BIG` on macOS (`spawn ENAMETOOLONG` on Windows, as reported in the issue), so no tags are replaced and the pull never completes.

## Root cause

- `Repository.handleTagConflict()` (`repository.ts`) interpolated `tags.join(', ')` into the modal message, so the message size grows with the number of conflicting tags.
- `Repository.fetchTags()` (`git.ts`) appended one `refs/tags/<tag>:refs/tags/<tag>` refspec per tag to a single `git fetch` command line. Large tag sets exceed the OS command-line limit (32K characters on Windows, `ARG_MAX` on macOS/Linux).

## Fix

- The message lists at most 5 tag names. When there are more, it uses a separate localized string, `... conflicting tag(s): {0} and {1} more. ...`. That string uses only placeholders, so no localized fragments are concatenated. For ≤ 5 tags the existing string is unchanged.
- `fetchTags()` splits the refspecs with `splitInChunks(refspecs, MAX_CLI_LENGTH)` and runs one `git fetch [--force] <remote> <chunk>` per chunk. This is the same pattern other multi-path commands in `git.ts` (for example `add`) already use. `--force` now comes before the remote so it applies to every chunk. Small tag sets still run a single `git fetch`, and everything still runs inside the existing `Operation.Pull`.

## Validation

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm run gulp compile-extension:git` | ✅ passed (0 errors) |
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/git/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | ✅ passed |
| `pnpm run oxlint extensions/git/src/git.ts extensions/git/src/repository.ts` | ✅ passed (2 files, no findings) |
| `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite git` | ✅ 91 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing |
| `validate-ui-scenario` on a Code OSS dev build (`--dev`, throwaway profile, scratch repo under `<tmp>`), fix reverted | ✅ bug reproduced (all 4 steps assert the buggy behaviour) |
| Same scenario with the fix | ✅ all 4 steps pass |

No unit test was added because no pure function was changed or extracted. The chunking reuses the existing `splitInChunks` helper.

## Evidence

I recorded a side-by-side video (BEFORE on `main` on the left, AFTER with this fix on the right, aligned by step) plus before/after screenshots of the dialog and the result, all with the validate-ui-scenario harness. I can share them on request. Each step asserts on the DOM or on the repository through `git` CLI, not on the screenshots alone. Button visibility is measured by intersecting each button with every clipping ancestor and hit-testing its centre.

**Step 2: Run "Git: Pull", and the tag conflict modal opens**

- Before: `BUG: message length 532634 chars; button visibility: Always Replace Local Tag(s) 62%, Cancel 62%, Replace Local Tag(s) 62% - the tag list squeezes the buttons out of the dialog.`
- After: `FIXED: message length 503 chars; button visibility: Always Replace Local Tag(s) 100%, Cancel 100%, Replace Local Tag(s) 100%.` The message reads "Unable to pull from remote repository due to conflicting tag(s): release/v1.00001.0-…, …, release/v1.00005.0-… and 7495 more. Would you like to resolve the conflict by replacing the local tag(s)?"

**Step 3: Choose "Replace Local Tag(s)"**

- Before: the button is clipped at the dialog edge, so the scenario invokes it through the DOM to exercise the Replace path.
- After: the visible button is clicked with the mouse.

**Step 4: Result of replacing the local tags**

- Before: `BUG: "Git: spawn E2BIG". 0/7500 tags replaced; pull did not complete.` The SCM Graph still shows `main` at `B` with incoming `origin/main`.
- After: `FIXED: 7500/7500 local tags now match the remote and HEAD equals origin/main; no error dialog.` The SCM Graph shows `main` at `C`. The Git log shows 40 chunked `git fetch --force origin refs/tags/...` invocations followed by a successful `git pull --tags origin main`.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, fixed threshold, synchronous call path, and one remote fetch per chunk are explicit in code. Exact latency depends on transport and tag-name lengths, but the boundary multiplication and critical-path placement are certain; platform argument limits only affect which input sizes regress versus previously fail.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses and serialized remote fetch round trips
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Once the generated refspec text exceeds 30 KB, cost grows as ceil(total refspec characters / 30,000); every chunk starts and awaits another remote `git fetch`. For the documented 7,500-tag shape this is roughly 40 serial fetches.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Conflict resolution blocks the pull on repeated process startup and remote discovery/connection latency, producing substantially higher end-to-end pull latency on platforms whose native argument limit would have allowed fewer or one fetch.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, tag replacement issued one `git fetch` containing all conflicting-tag refspecs. That failed when the host command-line limit was exceeded, but on Linux and on macOS for inputs between 30 KB and the native limit it completed with one subprocess and one remote fetch.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The change applies the conservative 30 KB threshold on every OS and serially executes one remote fetch per chunk, including on hosts where the original command still fits under the actual process argument limit.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop at line 2527 invokes and awaits `this.exec([...args, ...chunk], spawnOptions)` once for every fixed-size chunk; the deleted code invoked `this.exec(args, spawnOptions)` exactly once after appending all refspecs.
Findings.Title: Keep forced tag replacement in one fetch
Findings.Impact: Repositories with hundreds or thousands of conflicting tags can wait through many serialized remote fetches before the original pull is retried. The regression is especially visible on Linux, where a refspec list far larger than 30 KB can still fit in one process invocation.
Findings.Evidence: `fetchTags` is reached synchronously while handling a pull/sync tag conflict, and `_pullAndHandleTagConflict` cannot retry the pull until it returns. `splitInChunks` groups solely by cumulative string length at 30,000 characters; the loop awaits each `exec`, so there is no coalescing and effective concurrency is one. Each command is `git fetch [--force] <remote> <chunk>`, crossing both subprocess and remote-network boundaries. The repository already supports supplying stdin through `SpawnOptions.input`, so the argument-size limit does not require repeated remote commands.
Findings.Recommendation: Pass the newline-separated refspecs through a single `git fetch --stdin` invocation using `spawnOptions.input` (while preserving `--force` and the remote), rather than splitting them into multiple remote fetches. This removes command-line-size pressure without multiplying subprocess and network boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull or sync with a small set of conflicting tags, followed by interactive replacement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initial `git pull --tags` fails with a tag conflict, the modal choice completes, one forced tag fetch completes, and then the pull retry completes. All of these steps are on the user-visible pull/sync critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial `git pull` that discovers and reports the tag conflict
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per pull attempt before conflict handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial pull occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must fail before conflict handling can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forced fetch of the conflicting tag refspecs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One when all generated refspecs total at most 30,000 characters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One forced fetch was issued with all refspecs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the pull is retried.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry of the original pull after tags are replaced
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same retry occurred after a successful forced fetch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number and length of conflicting tag names; with aggregate generated refspec text at or below 30,000 characters, effective fetch cardinality remains one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The forced fetch and pull retry are serialized by `await`; the changed chunk loop yields one iteration for this case.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Warm versus cold object storage may change how much pack data Git transfers, but does not change command cardinality; there is no coalescing or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `splitInChunks` yields one chunk and the loop executes one awaited `exec`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Git transport and repository object state determine absolute duration, but the changed behavior does not increase boundary count for this size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for small inputs. The modal now allocates/renders only up to five tag names, and forced-fetch cardinality remains unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull or sync with enough conflicting tags for generated refspecs to exceed 30 KB
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the initial pull reports conflicts and any modal choice completes, every chunked forced fetch runs serially before the final pull retry can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial `git pull --tags` that returns all conflicting tags
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete and fail before replacement starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forced fetches for chunks of conflicting-tag refspecs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Changed from one attempted fetch to N=ceil(refspec characters/30,000) serial fetches. On Unix inputs below the native argument budget, the old one-fetch command succeeded; on lower-limit hosts or larger inputs it failed before completing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A single `git fetch [--force] <remote> <all refspecs>` was executed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All N fetches block the final pull retry; every additional chunk adds process startup and remote round-trip latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One after all forced-fetch chunks succeed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The retry followed the one forced fetch when that command fit the host argument limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cannot begin until the full serial fan-out completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Aggregate generated refspec length, which includes each tag name twice plus `refs/tags/` prefixes. Effective forced-fetch cardinality is ceil(total refspec characters / 30,000); the 7,500 long-tag scenario is approximately 40 chunks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one forced fetch at a time because each `this.exec` is awaited inside the loop. There is no shared batch beyond each 30 KB chunk and no overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache changes cardinality. A warm Git object database can reduce transferred pack bytes, but each chunk still starts a subprocess and performs remote discovery/connection work; failures stop later chunks and there is no result coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the fixed 30 KB grouping, awaited loop, remote `git fetch` command, and blocking pull call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of hundreds or thousands of conflicting tags and per-fetch transport latency varies. Severity is medium because the exact delay is environment-dependent, while the serial boundary multiplication is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary-fanout regression on hosts whose native argument limit exceeds 30 KB. A single stdin-fed fetch can preserve command-size safety without multiplying remote calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the conflict confirmation for a very large tag set
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The failed pull's stderr is parsed, the localized message is constructed, and `showErrorMessage` renders before user replacement can proceed. With automatic replacement configured, this modal path is skipped.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and length of conflicting tags in stderr. Message construction and rendering now include at most five names, while extraction of all tag names from the pre-existing stderr remains linear.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous message construction precedes one awaited modal display; no subprocess, filesystem, database, IPC, or network boundary is added by the changed message branch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used; repeated conflicts reconstruct the bounded message each time.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added `slice(0, 5).join` directly caps the localized message payload.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Renderer cost varies, but the changed message payload is bounded and strictly smaller for more than five tags.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This hunk removes unbounded message serialization/rendering work and does not create a new expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. One medium-confidence-independent, high-mechanism-confidence boundary-fanout issue was submitted: fixed 30 KB chunking serializes one otherwise-valid Unix fetch into many remote fetches. The modal truncation is a performance improvement, and small tag sets retain one-fetch behavior.
